questions.q: What do mirror neurons make us do when we see someone using a product in an ad?
a: Mimic the action and want the product
Ignore the ad's central message
Feel suspicious of the brand
Remember the ad but not buy
questions.why: Lesson 1 says our brains react to watching an action much as if we performed it, which nudges us to copy and buy.

questions.q: How does dopamine affect our shopping?
a: It makes us spend more than we planned
It makes us compare prices carefully
It reduces our desire for status
It helps us resist advertising
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes dopamine as a pleasure hormone present while shopping that can push us to overspend.

questions.q: Why do fear-based advertisements work, according to the summary?
a: We want relief, and the product is shown as safety
We enjoy feeling frightened by media
Fear makes us forget earlier purchases
Fear lowers the price we are willing to pay
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that ads pair a fear with the product as the escape from it, offering security.

questions.q: What did Lyndon B. Johnson's campaign ad use to win support?
a: A nuclear explosion playing on fear of war
A happy family enjoying a picnic
A famous actor endorsing him
A catchy song that became a hit
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the daisy ad, where a child's idyllic scene is shattered by a nuclear blast.

questions.q: In the summary's broader definition, what counts as subliminal messaging?
a: Anything that influences us without our noticing
Only messages flashed for milliseconds
Any advertisement shown late at night
Testimonials from real customers
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the tactic covers anything that gets us to buy without us realizing we are being influenced.
